original_question: Suppose a closed manifold (M, g) admits a non-zero (1, 1)-tensor field that is self-adjoint with respect to g, parallel and nilpotent.
target_in_paper: Section 12, "How to reconstruct a metric from its geodesics," specifically Question 12.0.1 in the final arXiv v3 / ETDS version; the same wording appears as Question 12.0.3 in the earlier submitted-version PDF. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the full hypothesis of the paper's open problem: a closed manifold with a nonzero (1,1)-tensor field that is self-adjoint with respect to g, parallel, and nilpotent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: The draft omits the actual question being asked: whether the manifold or its double cover admits a nonzero light-like parallel vector field. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The surrounding paragraph places this in the pseudo-Riemannian/semi-Riemannian setting, not the positive-definite Riemannian one; this is implicit from the sentence beginning "In the pseudo-Riemannian case" and from the light-like conclusion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

To be stand-alone, the tensor should be identified as an endomorphism field A in Gamma(End(TM)); the nearby context discusses such a (1,1)-tensor arising from affinely equivalent metrics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Parallel should be stated as parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection of g. The surrounding discussion explicitly refers to the Levi-Civita connection. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
To remove ambiguity, self-adjoint should be spelled out as g(A X, Y) = g(X, A Y) for all vector fields X, Y; nilpotent should be spelled out as A^N = 0 for some integer N >= 2.
The phrase "light-like parallel vector field" should be made explicit as a nonzero vector field V with nabla V = 0 and g(V,V) = 0.
The possibility of passing to a double cover is essential in the paper's formulation and should not be dropped. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The motivating scope is the special one-eigenvalue (hence zero-eigenvalue / nilpotent) case in the pseudo-Riemannian theory of affinely equivalent metrics; this nearby context explains why the question is asked and keeps the reformulation paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a closed pseudo-Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection nabla. Assume there exists a nonzero endomorphism field A in Gamma(End(TM)) such that g(A X, Y) = g(X, A Y) for all vector fields X,Y, nabla A = 0, and A is nilpotent (equivalently, A^N = 0 for some integer N >= 2). Must M, or at least a double cover of M, admit a nonzero light-like parallel vector field V (that is, nabla V = 0 and g(V,V) = 0)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the unique open problem in the paper containing the unusual combination of hypotheses "self-adjoint," "parallel," and "nilpotent" for a (1,1)-tensor. The immediately preceding context explains that this question arises in the pseudo-Riemannian case of affinely equivalent metrics: the associated parallel self-adjoint tensor has generalized eigenspace foliations, and the especially interesting unresolved case is when it has only one eigenvalue, which may be taken to be 0. The paper then states that all known closed-manifold examples are built from light-like parallel vector fields and formulates exactly the question above. So the nearest official formulation is Section 12, Question 12.0.1, not any broader neighboring problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
